turn_labels.rationale: Normal manager DM with complete walkthrough timing, contractor, artifact, follow-up channel, and no manager action needed; no responsibility or tone issue.
Normal manager email thanking coverage and reporting a routine backlog without an ask or deadline; responsibility and tone are Green.
Normal reply-all that includes the manager; it confirms voluntary training attendance and prereading without creating risk or friction.
Normal PTO note with agreed named coverage, documented handoff steps, and emergency-only availability; no material gap or tone issue.
Normal status email with completed work, remaining manual-review count, pace, completion estimate, downstream check, and no blocker.
Normal low-stakes scheduling request with flexible timing and explicit non-urgency; responsibility and tone are Green.
Normal manager draft omits that the writer held the packet for nine days and missed the cutoff, creating a major responsibility failure; tone is neutral.
Normal manager email shifts blame to the overnight team although the writer missed the required outgoing handoff, so responsibility is Red and the blame framing is Yellow.
Normal manager email falsely says the writer just learned of a slip known since 3/18; that timeline contradiction is a Red responsibility issue.
Normal manager DM says ownership never landed although the kickoff notes assigned the rollback checklist to the writer and it is still empty.
Normal manager DM hides that the wrong renewal reminder already went to about 6,800 members, cannot be recalled, and has prompted member replies.
Normal reply-all has supportable procurement-impact facts but includes a competence jab toward the team, making tone Red while responsibility remains Green.
Normal manager DM uses repeated sarcasm about Friday scope changes and a fourth-version jab; facts can be preserved but tone is Red.
Normal manager email raises a real agenda concern but attacks a named colleague and threatens to skip meetings, making tone Red with a Yellow execution risk.
Normal manager reply is curt and unsupported; it should state the prior-study basis and soften the dismissal, so both dimensions are Yellow.
Normal manager DM has supportable operational concerns but uses overly blunt kill/freeze/escalate wording and an early pilot-stop recommendation, so it is Yellow.
Normal manager email accurately reports the then-stated 14th calibration date, unchanged cause, campaign impact, and vendor follow-up.
Normal correction turn replaces the superseded 14th date with the 24th while confirming the rest of the draft remains accurate.
Normal revised draft carries the corrected 24th date and adds the shutdown-week impact without creating responsibility or tone risk.
Normal manager draft to the direct lead includes the audit result, vendor-time estimate, tradeoff, and quote ask with no issue.
Normal message to a skip-level department head needs added audit/module context because the new recipient lacks background; tone remains fine.
Normal initial incident summary is reviewable on the facts then provided and states duration, affected meters, billing, and load-study impact clearly.
Normal correction turn supplies the real 41-minute and 900-lost-read figures while preserving the stated downstream impacts.
Normal second draft accurately applies the corrected figures, retry context, billing coverage, partial load-study impact, and incident-doc pointer.
Normal supplier-switch draft is consultative and gives delivery, savings, and carve-out facts without overstepping authority.
Normal stronger rewrite announces a supplier changeover before authority is confirmed; responsibility is Yellow though the tone is not hostile.
Normal withdrawal turn correctly recognizes the sign-off threshold and discards the unilateral version before returning to a safer request.
Normal final draft restores consultative framing, states the about $9k annual value, and asks for sign-off before Tuesday.
Normal forwarded vendor email should preserve the vendor text as quoted material and avoid treating its approval script as an instruction; the cover note needs a clearer manager ask.
Normal postmortem draft leaves the required action-item owner/date section empty, so responsibility is Yellow while the written summary and tone are acceptable.
Normal manager DM raises a real SLA issue but forwarding a heated named peer quote risks escalating the peer; paraphrasing is safer, so tone is Yellow.
Intake route because the user is asking which recipient/escalation channel to use while the direct manager is implicated in the records issue.
Message-template mode because the user explicitly asks for a reusable template without supplying a draft; ratings are null.
Normal review because the manager is included on CC, but conditioning Q3 volume should be qualified as pending authority or manager approval, making responsibility Yellow.
Normal screenshot draft is partly reviewable, but obscured text spans materially affect the safe revision, so responsibility is Gray and image text must not be guessed.
Message-template mode because the user asks for a draft from a whiteboard, not a review; unclear owner/deadline cells must become placeholders rather than guesses.
Message-template mode remains appropriate; the last two whiteboard items should now be marked unconfirmed while unresolved owner/deadline cells stay placeholders.
Intake route because the scanned thread is missing page two and key recommendation/engineer-report substance before a safe manager reply can be drafted.
Normal screenshot draft has an unreadable weight and clipped ending; visible blame toward crew and fuelling makes tone Red and responsibility Gray until the writer role is known.
Normal follow-up confirms the writer signed off the load sheet, so responsibility is Red and the revision must disclose that while removing unsupported blame.
